answer: A bond-backed attestation trellis resists Sybils: each agent stakes tokens that lock into an interlocking graph of mutual vouches, so creating a fake identity costs real capital instead of a free account. New identities start at the nadir of trust with tiny transaction limits, and an unverified island of agents cannot trade with the main economy until established members vouch for them and risk their own stake. Attackers must therefore fund every fake at full price.
